answer: A farm running 177 keys thus pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. Because the ocean stake is held until the spiral settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the signal audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 34% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
